title: Marketing Manager Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Learn how to convert a marketing manager salary from hourly to annual using the 38-hour week, plus tax, super, and award rates. Includes ABS benchmarks and Fair Work guidelines.
salarySummary: Based on ABS Average Weekly Earnings, a typical full-time marketing manager salary is around $108,352 per year (assuming 38 hours per week), but actual rates depend on the applicable award or agreement.

faqs.q: What is the average marketing manager salary in Australia?
faqs.a: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings are $2,083.70 per week, which equates to about $108,352 per year (38 hours × 52 weeks). This is a broad benchmark; actual marketing manager salaries vary by industry, experience, and location. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to calculate your own rate.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (typically 38 for full-time) and then by 52. For example, $50 per hour × 38 × 52 = $98,800 per year. Superannuation of 12% is paid on top of this amount. Remember that award or enterprise agreement rates may differ from the National Minimum Wage.

faqs.q: Does the National Minimum Wage apply to marketing managers?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. Most marketing managers are covered by an award such as the Professional Employees Award or a registered agreement, which set higher minimum rates. Check your award using the [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Calculator.

bodyMarkdown:
## Marketing Manager Salary: From Hourly to Annual

If you're a marketing manager negotiating a new role or reviewing your current pay, understanding how an hourly rate translates into annual salary is essential. In Australia, the standard full-time working week is 38 hours, and the formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 = annual gross pay**. This article explains the calculation, the role of the National Minimum Wage and awards, and how tax and super affect your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked each week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time marketing manager working 38 hours per week:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual figure is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.40. However, a marketing manager salary is typically much higher. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings are $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That gives an annual benchmark of $2,083.70 × 52 = $108,352.40.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the ABS benchmark: $2,083.70 per week × 2 = $4,167.40 per fortnight before tax.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage at $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026). This is the minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most marketing managers, however, are covered by the **Professional Employees Award** or a similar industry award. Award rates are higher than the national minimum and include classifications based on skill level and responsibility. Always check the relevant award using the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual marketing manager, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For award/agreement-free casuals, that means $33.05 per hour. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this works. Our [timesheet](/) calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically – never type a rate that already includes the loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is not deducted from your salary; it is paid on top. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual salary is $108,352, your employer must contribute an additional $13,002 to your super fund (unless you exceed the cap). See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

### Tax and Medicare

Your gross annual salary is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. The 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Using the ABS benchmark salary of $108,352:

- Tax: $4,020 + 0.30 × ($108,352 – $45,000) = $4,020 + $19,005.60 = $23,025.60
- Medicare: 2% × $108,352 = $2,167.04
- Total deductions: $25,192.64
- Estimated take-home pay: $108,352 – $25,192.64 = $83,159.36 per year

Note: The Medicare levy reduction thresholds used here are the 2025–26 single figures, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised calculation.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page where you can enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual, tick the casual loading box – the calculator adds 25% on top. The result shows your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. It assumes 38 hours per week, the same rate every week, and no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice.

### Key Points to Remember

- The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour; award rates for marketing managers are higher.
- Casual employees receive a 25% loading.
- Super is 12% on top of ordinary earnings, up to the cap.
- Tax and Medicare are deducted from your gross pay.
- The ABS average weekly earnings provide a useful benchmark, but your actual marketing manager salary depends on your award, agreement, and negotiation.

For more detailed award rates, visit the [reference tables](/data). To check your specific industry award, use the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Guides.
